note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, lighting answer and opening time below comes from the City of San Antonio's own pages: the Parks & Recreation pickleball directory, and each park's own page for the count sentence. The City states no price and no surface anywhere, and where it is silent this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
Seven of the eight park pages list "Regular Parking Spaces" and "Handicapped Parking Spaces" among their amenities: Fairchild, Garza, Monterrey, Normoyle, Oak Haven, Pittman-Sullivan and Tejeda. That is the whole of it: no capacity, no fee, no permit, and nothing on where the lot sits relative to the courts. Palm Heights Park's amenity list has no parking line at all.

Restrooms are the other thing to plan around. The City writes "Restrooms" at Normoyle, Pittman-Sullivan and Tejeda, and "Portable Toilet" at Garza, Monterrey and Oak Haven. Fairchild and Palm Heights list neither. Oak Haven's page also prints two addresses: "16400 Parkstone" under its pickleball entry and "2215 Rest Haven Dr." in its contact block. The City's directory uses Rest Haven, and so does this page.
slots.peak_hours:
San Antonio publishes one clock for all eight venues. Every park on the City's pickleball directory carries the same park hours, 5 a.m. to 11 p.m., seven days a week, and the City's park directory states that "All other courts are available during park hours."

How much of that window is usable after dark is answered at only two venues. Fairchild's eighteen courts and Tejeda's six are "lighted" in the City's own count sentences, which is twenty-four of the forty-three verified courts. For the other six parks the caveat applies: "Some courts are not lighted." Several of those pages do say whether the tennis court is lit, but those sentences are about tennis and are not carried across.

Everything is first come, first served, and the City publishes nothing about when any court is busy. Fairchild's page warns that "Special events and scheduled activities may affect court usage and open hours".
slots.surface_condition:
The City of San Antonio names a surface for a pickleball court nowhere. The word "asphalt" appears on these pages three times and none of them is about pickleball: Garza's trail, Monterrey's trail, and a 1929 contract for "cold rolled asphalt tennis courts" in Palm Heights Park. So all forty-three verified courts read as not stated on surface.

What the City does write is where the courts are. Its count sentences carry "outdoor" at six parks and "indoor" at Palm Heights, which puts thirty-five courts outdoors and two inside. Tejeda is the exception: its line is "There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts.", lighted but not outdoor, so its six are left as neither. Nothing says whether a court is dedicated to pickleball or lined onto a tennis court.
slots.local_scene:
Forty-three verified courts across eight City parks, and the arithmetic is lopsided: Fairchild Park holds eighteen of them, Monterrey eight, Tejeda six, and the other five parks share eleven. Fairchild's eighteen lit outdoor courts are one of the largest single-venue counts on this site, and the largest anywhere here where the operator states that every court is both lit and outdoor. San Antonio is the second Texas city on this site after Austin and the first in Bexar County.

What San Antonio does not say is the price. No page states a charge or the absence of one, so no venue here is called free. For beginners the City offers one way in: "Take a Pickleball 101 class through the Fitness in the Park program, equipment provided."

Two listed venues are not published. Piazza Italia Park has one outdoor court at an address, "500 Columbus", that neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap can find. Hamilton Community Center has a Saturday pickleball window and no court count anywhere.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts under lights
best_for.text: Fairchild Park has eighteen lighted outdoor pickleball courts in one City sentence, alongside ten lighted outdoor tennis courts, on the east side at 1214 E Crockett St. The courts are open during park hours, 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, first come, first served. Eighteen courts under lights until eleven is a rotation that absorbs almost any number of players; nothing else in San Antonio is in the same class.

best_for.heading: Best if you want lights on the south side
best_for.text: Tejeda Park's six courts are the only other lit pickleball in the City's record: "There are 6 lighted, pickleball courts." There are restrooms and lit tennis courts too, in a park of 8.76 acres on the south side that the City renamed for Congressman Frank Tejeda in 1996. Six is enough for a rotation, and 11 p.m. park hours make an after-work game a stated possibility rather than a hope.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to play indoors
best_for.text: Palm Heights Park has the City's only indoor pickleball count: "There are 2 indoor pickleball courts." on a 1.72-acre park on the south-west side whose history records a gymnasium added in 1977. Two courts is a game rather than a rotation, and the City publishes no separate gym schedule for pickleball, only park hours of 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does San Antonio have?
faqs.a: We have verified 43 across eight City parks: 18 at Fairchild, 8 at Monterrey, 6 at Tejeda, 4 at Normoyle, 2 each at Garza, Palm Heights and Pittman-Sullivan, and 1 at Oak Haven. The City also lists Piazza Italia Park and Hamilton Community Center, so the real number is at least 44.

faqs.q: Which San Antonio courts have lights?
faqs.a: Fairchild Park's 18 and Tejeda Park's 6, because "lighted" is in the City's own count sentence at both. At the other six parks the City says nothing about pickleball lighting, so those are recorded as unknown.
Park hours, 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. every day, at all eight venues. The one stated exception is Hamilton Community Center, not published here: Saturday, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.

sources.evidence: The City's pickleball directory page. Intro: "There are several indoor and outdoor pickleball courts at our parks across the city. These are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Some courts are not lighted." Then "Courts at Hamilton Community Center are available Saturday, 10 a.m. - 2 p.m." and "All other courts are available during park hours." and "Want to learn how to play? Take a Pickleball 101 class through the Fitness in the Park program, equipment provided." Under "Directory" it says "11 Result(s) Found" and lists ten entries, each park with its address and "Park Hours: Sunday - Saturday: 5 a.m. - 11 p.m."; Normoyle Park additionally "Pool Hours: Saturday & Sunday: 1 - 8 p.m."; Hamilton Community Center at "10700 Nacogdoches Rd., San Antonio, TX 78217" with "Facility Hours: Monday - Thursday: 10 a.m. - 8 p.m. Friday: 2 - 6 p.m. Saturday: 10 a.m. - 4 p.m." and no count; Piazza Italia Park at "500 Columbus, San Antonio, TX 78207". "Page 1 of 2", and page two returns the same ten. Snapshot: data/sources/san-antonio/pickleball.html
sources.not_stated: Any court count, any price, any surface, which courts are the unlit ones, and the eleventh result.
